clue.text: Cruise by Hollywood location after box office draw

indicators.note: the Hollywood location comes after the box office letters in the answer

parts.note: Tom Cruise, the film star
Hollywood is in LA, Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A film star in Hollywood, following his box-office pull.
explanation.walkthrough: A tombola is a British raffle in which tickets are drawn from a revolving drum, common at fêtes.
explanation.definitionFit: A tombola is a type of lottery or raffle, so it is a prize draw.

clue.text: Top model's rear

parts.note: the Ford Model T car
the rump is the hindquarters

explanation.surface: A leading model's backside, perhaps as a tabloid headline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' is a verb: to trump a card or an achievement is to beat it.
explanation.definitionFit: To trump is to outdo or beat, as a trump card beats others, so to top.

clue.text: Swallow one drink

parts.note: a martin is a bird of the swallow family
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone gulps down a single drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' looks like a verb about drinking; it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a cocktail of gin or vodka with vermouth.

clue.text: Knocked over small stool, silly me!

indicators.note: in a down clue, knocked over means turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: stool in the medical sense of faeces

explanation.surface: Someone tips over a little stool and blames their own clumsiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Oops is an exclamation admitting a small mistake, just like saying silly me.

clue.text: Liar Boris in NHS U-turns? Terrible time

indicators.note: the U-turns phrase suggests changes of direction, so the letters are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the U from U-turns

explanation.surface: Political commentary: a dishonest Boris Johnson reverses his NHS policies during a dreadful period.
explanation.walkthrough: The U of 'U-turns' is part of the fodder; 'turns' alone signals the rearrangement. The NHS is Britain's National Health Service.
explanation.definitionFit: Annus horribilis is Latin for a horrible year, popularised by the Queen in 1992.

clue.text: Cruel French here? You must provide cover

indicators.note: the word for you must wrap around and shelter the word for here

parts.note: vous is French for you; the 'French' carries over
ici is French for here

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about French, followed by an instruction to someone to give protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' governs both words: ICI is French for here, VOUS French for you.
explanation.definitionFit: Vicious and cruel are synonyms, both describing deliberate malice or savagery.

clue.text: Meeting once Covid-free: end virtually working

indicators.note: working means being worked into shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: virtually means almost, so all but the final letter of end

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark about pandemic meetings ending their online phase once Covid is gone.
explanation.definitionFit: A video conference is a meeting held over a video link between remote participants.

clue.text: Continually drag donkey behind tethers

indicators.note: in a down clue the donkey is placed after (below) the tethers

parts.note: to chain is to tether
moke is a British slang word for a donkey

explanation.surface: Someone keeps pulling a donkey along behind its tethers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drag' means a puff on a cigarette, not a pull; moke is British slang for a donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: To chain-smoke is to light one cigarette from the last, taking drag after drag.

clue.text: Hole clear in golf

parts.note: open means clear, unobstructed
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A hole that is clear in a game of golf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hole' looks like a golf hole; it is the definition, meaning a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening is a hole or gap through which something can pass.

clue.text: Slumped outside hospital, exhausted

indicators.note: the slumping word sits outside the hospital letter

parts.note: sagged means drooped or slumped
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A worn-out person collapses outside a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: Shagged out is British slang for exhausted; the word also has a vulgar sense that the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, shagged or shagged out means utterly tired, worn out.

clue.text: Shot under pine makes green

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or ruined, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rifle shot fired beneath a pine tree turns something green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' looks like a gunshot but signals the rearrangement; 'green' looks like a colour but means not ripe.
explanation.definitionFit: Green fruit is fruit that has not yet ripened, an everyday sense of the colour word.

clue.text: An English painter recalled scene

indicators.note: called back, so the letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, a painter in crossword convention

explanation.surface: An English artist remembered a scene he painted.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is the place where events unfold, a scene of action or activity.

clue.text: Broadcast following prince and partner

indicators.note: the broadcast word comes after the prince's letter

parts.note: to air something is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: A programme aired after a prince and his partner appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: To pair someone is to match them up with another, that is, to partner them.

clue.text: Breathtaking time in afternoon, going off

parts.note: A is taken as short for afternoon, as in the a of p.m. readings; a loose abbreviation

indicators.note: the time letter is placed within the afternoon letter joined to the going-off word

parts.note: an alarm going off is sounding

explanation.surface: An astonishing afternoon moment when an alarm starts ringing.
explanation.walkthrough: The afternoon letter A is an unusual abbreviation that the blog's commenters questioned; an alarm going off is SOUNDING, and T goes in after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Something astounding takes your breath away, so the two adjectives are close synonyms.

clue.text: Conservative to go briefly to north-east for break

indicators.note: shortened, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to travel is to go
NE is the compass abbreviation

explanation.surface: A Tory politician heads briefly to north-east England for a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' looks like a holiday but is the verb, as in breaking a rule.
explanation.definitionFit: To contravene a law or rule is to break or violate it.

clue.text: American soldier on leave to look for escort

parts.note: a GI is a US soldier
to go is to leave
lo is an old word meaning look!

explanation.surface: A US serviceman on leave, hoping to find a companion.
explanation.definitionFit: A gigolo is a man paid to accompany or be the lover of a wealthy woman, a male escort.

clue.text: Some do gym, hoping to get back that's amazing

indicators.note: getting back means returning, so the run is read backwards
only some of the letters of the following words are used

parts.note: the run of letters taken from these words

explanation.surface: Gym-goers hoping to recover their former fitness.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is what someone says on seeing something astonishing, an idiom of surprise.

clue.text: Guide for better parking in line across street

indicators.note: the parking letter sits within the row word
the row word spans across the street letters too, holding both

parts.note: a tier is a row or line

explanation.surface: Directions for parking in a queue on the other side of a street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' here is one who bets, not 'more good'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipster offers betting tips, guiding a punter on which horse to back.

clue.text: American made child and daughter drink beer

indicators.note: the child and daughter take in the beer, as one takes in a drink

parts.note: a tot is a small child
ale is beer

explanation.surface: An American has his child and daughter drinking beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' is in the sense of added up to (two and two made four); the single L is the US spelling, hence 'American'.
explanation.definitionFit: Totaled, US spelling, means amounted to or came to, as numbers make a sum.

clue.text: Image of a lad on front of Attitude

parts.note: per means a, each, as in fifty pence a go
a son is a boy, a lad

indicators.note: takes the first letter of Attitude

explanation.surface: A picture of a young man on the cover of Attitude, a gay lifestyle magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' works in the sense of 'ten pounds a head', meaning each; 'on' only orders the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A persona is the image or character someone presents to the world.

clue.text: Copying fine family silver cups

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: the silver letters hold the family word, as hands cup something

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
kin means family

explanation.surface: Making copies of a fine family's silver cups, perhaps for a forger.
explanation.definitionFit: Faking something means making a fraudulent imitation of it, a form of copying.

clue.text: Couples covering pillowcases after sleep: dirty ones need changing

indicators.note: these letters come after the sleep word

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep

indicators.note: only the pairs of letters at each end, the covering couples, are kept from the long word

parts.note: the word whose ends are used

explanation.surface: Domestic laundry: pairs of pillowcases after a night's sleep, the dirty ones needing a wash.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep only the two-letter 'couples' at each end of pillowcases, PI and ES.
explanation.definitionFit: Nappies are what babies wear (diapers in the US), and soiled ones must be changed.

clue.text: Worn out, the nurses scan unit for pressure

indicators.note: nurses means holds closely, so the word the cradles the other letters

parts.note: to scan a text is to read it
the bar is a unit of atmospheric pressure

explanation.surface: Exhausted, hospital nurses scan a ward for pressure sores.
explanation.definitionFit: Threadbare clothes are worn so thin that the threads show, so they are worn out.

clue.text: Copies recordings, missing the start

indicators.note: the recordings word loses its opening letter

parts.note: tapes are audio or video recordings

explanation.surface: A person duplicates recordings but loses their opening sections.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to mimic or imitate them, so apes means copies.

clue.text: Lay out section with page having margin

parts.note: an end is a boundary, the edge or margin of something

explanation.surface: Instructions to set out a section of a book with a page margin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay out' looks like typesetting but means paying out money.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay out money is to spend it, an idiomatic phrasal verb.

clue.text: Snake bites one without delay

indicators.note: the snake word takes the letter in its mouth

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake
a means one

explanation.surface: A snake strikes someone immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: ASAP is the abbreviation for as soon as possible, meaning immediately.

clue.text: Fail to keep old inside — it's immoral

indicators.note: the failing word holds the other letter
the old letter is placed within the failing word

parts.note: to lose is to fail, as in a contest

explanation.surface: A warning not to hide away old sins because they are immoral.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose here is the dated sense of promiscuous or dissolute in behaviour, hence immoral.

clue.text: Overwhelming hospital ultimately and gradually get worse

indicators.note: in the end, so the final letter of hospital

parts.note: to slide is to decline slowly

explanation.surface: A hospital patient's condition steadily deteriorates, overwhelmingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overwhelming' is an adjective here, as in an overwhelming election win.
explanation.definitionFit: A landslide is a crushing electoral victory, used attributively as in a landslide win.

clue.text: Knickers found in these?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an old word for underpants
second meaning: underwear is kept in the ... of a chest

explanation.walkthrough: The two readings overlap: underwear of this name is itself kept in a chest of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both old-fashioned underpants and the sliding boxes in a chest of furniture.

clue.text: Once modelled naked

parts.note: ex means former, once
a model poses for an artist

explanation.surface: Someone once posed for an artist without clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposed means uncovered and laid bare, so a body exposed is naked.
